title: The remaining dispute lies between individual doctors, not between the Schools
source_text: III. Quae vero circa quaestiones illas contentio superest, ut ex praecedentibus Thesibus liquere potest, non est proprie inter scholam & scholam; sed inter privatos Doctores qui, in utraque Schola, de hisce rebus varie sentiunt & Philosophantur. Quippe nulla prope sententia in una Schola circa haec obtinet, quae non habeat aliquos in altera Schola patronos. Et nulla saltem ab adversae Scholae Doctoribus rejicitur, quam domestici quoque aliqui non impugnent.
pass_a_gloss: But the contention which remains about those questions, as may be clear from the preceding Theses, is not properly between school and school; but between private Doctors who, in either School, think and Philosophize variously about these things. Indeed almost no opinion obtains in one School about these matters, which has not some patrons in the other School. And at least none is rejected by the Doctors of the opposite School, which some of its own also do not attack.
pass_b_english: As the earlier theses show, whatever dispute remains on those questions is not really between one school and the other. It is between individual teachers who, in both schools, think and reason about these matters in different ways.

Hardly any view on them prevails in one school without having some defenders in the other. And at least no view is rejected by teachers of the opposing school without being attacked as well by some teachers of its own school.

choices.why: Kept as in the preceding locus on free choice in general, so the Roman and Reformed accounts are compared in one vocabulary.
